allowed.name: @img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64
allowed.reason: LGPL-3.0-or-later, unused-at-runtime. Transitive platform binary of `sharp`, itself a transitive dependency of @huggingface/transformers (src/lib/nerPiiDetector.ts, client-side PII/NER detector, §1.6). @huggingface/transformers' package.json `exports` map routes the bundler/browser condition (what Vite resolves) to dist/transformers.web.js, NOT dist/transformers.node.cjs — confirmed by inspecting the installed package: the web build's bundler stubs `sharp` to an empty object at publish time (`// ignore-modules:sharp` directive, `var sharp_default = {}`) rather than importing it. `sharp` and its @img/sharp-libvips-* platform binaries are therefore never imported, bundled, or executed by our shipped browser code, and are not referenced anywhere in services/worker (grep-confirmed zero server-side usage) — inert transitive dependency-of-a-dependency in node_modules/package-lock.json only. No distribution, no relinking obligation triggered. Re-audit if @huggingface/transformers is ever imported server-side or its exports map changes on upgrade. Version moved 1.2.4->1.3.3 / 0.34.5->0.35.4 by the PR #2839 `sharp` override (Trivy CVE bump, Sekura Phase 2 H1/H2); the NOT-DISTRIBUTED reasoning is unchanged and the miniflare-only 1.3.1/0.35.2 band is gone because npm dedupes wrangler's nested copy onto the override. CTO review 2026-09-12.

allowed.name: libheif-js
allowed.reason: LGPL-3.0, browser-only. Transitive dependency of heic-decode (client-side HEIC/HEIF image decoding, F4 founder 22-format KPI). Used unmodified from the published npm tarball (wraps upstream libheif/libde265 as a self-contained wasm bundle — no fork, no patch). Isolated to the lazy 'vendor-heic' Vite chunk (see vite.config.ts manualChunks) and never inlined into the initial/main bundle, so the LGPL-3.0 relinking/swap obligation is satisfiable without shipping a static-linked main bundle. Third-party notices (LGPL-3.0 + GPLv3 texts, unmodified-source link) published at /legal/third-party-notices, linked from the public footer. Decode-only usage confirmed — no x265 (GPL-2.0) encoder evidence found in the wasm binary. See scripts/security/agents.md and PR remediating SCRUM license-denylist LGPL blind spot.
